notes: Bead Grid Studio v1.4.0 is a local-first, front-end-only fuse-bead pattern editor (Vite build, no backend, no accounts, no third-party API calls at runtime), so no stubs are needed. Toolchain: node 24.11.1 pinned in ./mise.toml (repo .nvmrc says 24, engines >=22.12). Rebuild with .ui-capture/build.sh: it runs `npm ci`, `vite build`, copies dist/ to .ui-capture/out, generates the seed project, and injects out/seed-draft.js. DATA: the app keeps one working project as a localStorage draft ('bead-grid-studio:draft:v2') and offers a 'Restore last unfinished pattern' button on start. .ui-capture/gen-pattern.mjs draws an original 52x52 pixel-art pattern ('年糕橘猫·红围巾（52板）', a ginger tabby cat in a red scarf sitting on a teal cushion with sparkles: 1,304 beads, 20 MARD colour codes) in the app's own project format (type 'bead-grid-studio', version 2, the same format as its .bead.json save files). It is board-size mode on a mini52 board, with code labels and rulers on, zoom 0.75 (what fit-to-view gives at 1440x900), and making-assistant progress where 6 colours are marked done (outline G8, eyes H16/H2, cushion C19/C22/C25) and the focus colour is A6. out/seed-draft.js (not part of the app source) writes that draft to localStorage if none exists, then clicks the app's own #restoreDraftBtn after init. That is the same reload -> restore flow covered by tests/e2e/i18n-growth.spec.js. .ui-capture/validate-seed.mjs checks the draft against the same rules as loadProjectFile(). MAIN AREAS: the top bar has the project title, upload, undo/redo, zoom, and export. The left panel has image import, smart conversion settings (process mode, max colours, merge strength, board size/profile) and save/load project. The centre has the bead grid canvas with rulers, per-cell colour codes, and a 10-cell major grid, plus a toolbar for brush, eraser, fill, mirror, rotate, despeckle, and replace colour. The right panel has the MARD 221 palette with search, plus material counts per colour (completed colours ticked) with copy/CSV export. Other parts are the 'pattern ready' bar, the making assistant, and the print/share-card dialogs. UI language follows the browser locale (en-US gives English; zh-CN, ja, ko, and fr are also available via ?lang=). A service worker is registered only over https, so it is inactive on a localhost http server.
